verdicts.text: R returns the same value for an anomaly placed BEFORE onset as for one placed AFTER it. A pre-onset anomaly has causal fraction zero by construction, so R is NOT an estimator of the causal fraction; it measures how tightly the anomaly is concentrated around the onset date. The original validation simulated only the post-onset structure and therefore could not detect this.

NO CLASS in CMIP6_ensemble (n=1888): the per-event surface response is unimodal (dip p=0.8460), one Gaussian component suffices (BIC-gap p=0.8650), and the whole distribution is a pure SHIFT of -0.511 sigma of the ordinary winter distribution (KS p=0.1907). 'Downward propagation' is a threshold on a continuum, not a population.

POOLING REFUSED. T1 passed, T2 4/7 betas agree. The observational arm stays at n=30 (1979 onward) and the pre-satellite extension is reported only as a sensitivity test, with the failing diagnostic stated.

Pre-specified global rule REFUSES pooling, and that verdict stands as the headline: the observational arm is n=30. Per-stratifier, 6/7 survive both checks (vT_pre30, vT_pre15, u10_post30, u10_post45, z100_post, AO_post) and the n=42 record is reported for those as a pre-registered sensitivity test, never as the primary number.

In ERA5 the published criterion gives a DW-minus-NDW contrast of -0.684 of which 96% is the selection term. A pure surface shift of -0.639 sigma applied to event-free dates gives a 74% pass rate against 69% observed -- so 'about two thirds propagate downward' is what ONE shifted population produces, with no classes in it.
UPPER BOUND on the structural share only; their r is between ensemble means, which suppresses the noise driving this bias.

The published criterion produces a DW-minus-NDW NAO contrast of -0.543; 86% of it is the selection term beta x dS. Residual -0.079 (p=0.443). For scale, ACP 26, 3723 (2026) publishes -0.850 from the same criterion.
